gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named clearance test on these printers: IgorsLab (Tim Kutzner) printed Sci3D's clearance fidget spinner on the Bambu Lab A1 mini and reported that all wheels down to a 0.15 mm gap turned straight off the plate without much force, and IgorsLab measured the A1 mini and the A1 at almost the same loudness, 55.3 and 55.1 dB(A) from about 40 cm.
standout_why: Rival pages compared: 3dprintgearlab.com (rank 1) has no measurements of its own and gives only a generic 0.2 mm design default credited to 'community design listings'. extruly.com (cited) gives slicer settings but says joint gap clearance is 'not specified', and its only noise figure is the ≤48 dB listing claim. aemind.com (cited) has no clearance, accuracy or noise figures, only P1S dragon print times from 3D Print Dood. tomshardware.com/3d-printing/best-3d-printers-for-kids-and-teens (cited) did not load: WebFetch returned only the page title. So I can't rule out that Tom's Hardware has a measurement, but none of the pages I could read has a measured clearance or noise result for the A1 mini or A1.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. On both printers, the gaps that fidget designs use by default (0.2 mm, sometimes 0.15 mm) came out moving, and the 0.05–0.10 mm gaps fused. Both printers can handle print-in-place fidgets as long as the model's gap is at least 0.15 mm, and 0.20–0.25 mm is the safe range. Noise doesn't separate them either (55.3 vs 55.1 dB(A), same reviewer, same distance), which contradicts one secondary site's claim that the mini is much quieter. So bed size (180 mm vs 256 mm) and budget decide between them, as ChatGPT's answer said.
candidates: Bambu Lab A1 mini Combo (AMS lite)

findings.label: Clearance fidget spinner (Sci3D) print-in-place result
findings.value: All wheels down to a 0.15 mm gap turned straight off the plate without much force
findings.source_title: IgorsLab: Bambu Lab A1 mini + AMS lite 3D printer in test (page 5, test prints)
findings.note: Tim Kutzner, IgorsLab, published 2023-12-13. Quote: 'all wheels up to 0.15mm tolerance could be moved directly without much force.' The article does not say which tighter wheels, if any, stayed fused, or which filament the spinner used.

findings.label: Clearance fidget spinner (Sci3D) print-in-place result
findings.value: Wheels down to a 0.15 mm gap turned without much force
findings.source_title: IgorsLab: Bambu Lab A1 + AMS lite 3D-Drucker im Test (Seite 5)
findings.note: Tim Kutzner, IgorsLab, published 2024-08-22, updated 2025-05-31. Quote: 'alle Rädchen bis bin zu 0,15mm Toleranz konnten ohne große Krafteinwirkung direkt bewegt werden'. The sentence on this A1 review page still names the 'A1 mini', so it may have been carried over from the mini review. Treat it as weaker evidence for the A1. The English A1 page returned 403.

findings.label: Print-in-place clearance ladder, PLA
findings.value: 0.05–0.10 mm fused or would not move; 0.15 mm moved with friction; 0.20–0.25 mm moved smoothly; 0.30 mm loose
findings.source_title: Fab Academy 2026, Kochi: Mishael Sharaf, Week 5 'Clearance and Tolerance (PLA on Bambu Lab A1)'
findings.note: Named student test in a Fab Lab, not a magazine lab. One print, PLA. The author concludes about 0.20 mm is best for print-in-place. The page has no date beyond 'Copyright 2026'.

findings.label: Print-in-place joint clearance test
findings.value: 0.10 mm joint 'could barely move within the socket'; 0.35 mm moved much more freely; movement increased with clearance
findings.source_title: Fab Academy 2026, Charlotte: Week05 Student group assignment (Yian Hu clearance test)
findings.note: Named student test (Yian Hu), tested 0.10–0.35 mm. Material not stated. Page last updated 2026-02-25.

findings.label: Noise while printing
findings.value: 55.3 dB(A) at about 40 cm from the front
findings.source_title: IgorsLab: Bambu Lab A1 mini + AMS lite 3D-Drucker im Test (Seite 6, Fazit)
findings.note: Tim Kutzner, published 2023-12-13. Quote: 'In etwa 40cm Abstand zur geschlossenen Front sind beim aktiven Betrieb 55,3 dB(A) Lautheit messbar.' The 'closed front' wording is from the article, though the A1 mini is an open-frame printer. Compare Bambu's listing claim of ≤48 dB in silent mode, which extruly repeats.

findings.label: Noise while printing
findings.value: 55.1 dB(A) at about 40 cm from the front
findings.source_title: IgorsLab: Bambu Lab A1 + AMS lite 3D-Drucker im Test (Seite 6, Fazit)
findings.note: Tim Kutzner, published 2024-08-22. Same reviewer and the same 40 cm method as the A1 mini figure. The difference from the mini is 0.2 dB(A), which is nothing you would hear.
